title: Federated Identity: the secretless agent
lede: An external token issuer the agent authenticates against instead of holding a key: expected iss, aud bound to a specific door, subject pinning, JWKS URI, max token lifetime, required claims. Nothing to leak, rotate, or commit.

nodes.label: JWKS URI
sub: public keys to verify the JWT

nodes.label: Gateway: verify + grant
sub: grant gated on claims, e.g. act.sub = agent id

nodes.label: Refused
sub: rebuilding 0 key(s): no key behind the NHI

steps.title: The platform mints the token
steps.what: The agent presents a platform-issued JWT — a Kubernetes service account, a GitHub Actions OIDC token, SPIFFE, or a PingFederate-issued token. There is no secret to leak, rotate, or accidentally commit.

steps.title: The NHI pins down what to trust
steps.what: Expected iss, mandatory aud bound to a specific door, subject pinning, a JWKS URI, a max token lifetime (needed because self-signing workloads choose their own exp), and required claims — e.g. GitHub repository + workflow.

steps.title: A key still backs the identity
steps.what: An NHI does not authenticate anyone by itself: it needs a key behind it (watch the gateway log tell 'rebuilding 0 key(s)') and a grant. The key's custodian is the NHI — and you must never set both a key-level WorkloadIdentity and an NHI custodian: the API refuses.

steps.title: Claims gate the grant
steps.what: PolicyRule.RequiredClaims gates what the token may do — for on-behalf-of flows, act.sub must equal the agent id, so the grant knows exactly which key, which repo, which human delegated.

steps.title: The gateway decides
steps.what: The gateway pulls the platform's public keys from the JWKS URI, verifies the JWT against the NHI's expected issuer, audience, subject, claims and lifetime, then applies the grant. Any miss is a refusal, not a downgrade.
